title: Finding Bugs in RTL Descriptions: High-Level Synthesis to the Rescue
problem: Manual RTL design based on behavioral C/C++ descriptions is time-consuming and error-prone. Finding bugs in manually designed hardware is tedious because designers must rely on extensive simulations that generate large waveforms requiring thorough scrutiny.
motivation: Automating bug detection in RTL designs can significantly reduce development time and improve design quality.
method: The approach leverages High-Level Synthesis (HLS) to generate reference RTL implementations from behavioral specifications, then compares these HLS-generated implementations against manually designed RTL to identify discrepancies and bugs. This uses HLS as a verification oracle, eliminating the need for exhaustive manual waveform analysis.
key_novelty: Using HLS-generated RTL as an automated reference to detect bugs in manual hardware designs without extensive simulation.
contributions: Framework for leveraging HLS as a bug-detection tool for manual RTL implementations
Automated comparison methodology between HLS-generated and manually designed RTL
Reduction of debugging effort through HLS-based verification
Demonstration of improved hardware design quality assurance
primary_theme: HLS-based automated bug detection for RTL
